title: Embeddable SDK Shuttle Quickstart and Fallback Lab
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview

Shuttle is an opinionated, lightweight embeddable SDK pattern designed for client-side or edge-hosted integrations that need a hybrid embeddings->generation workflow with robust fallback behavior. This playbook explains the Shuttle adapter pattern, provides a step-by-step quickstart, shows recommended default configs, and documents canonical fixes for the top support issues we see in Shuttle-style integrations.

Goals

- Provide a safe, minimal dependency for product teams needing: local prefetch + cache, streaming fallbacks, and predictable token budgets.
- Standardize telemetry and cohort signals so Support and DevX can reproduce problems quickly.
- Give clear operator runbook for migrating from a direct Redwood API client to Shuttle.

When to use Shuttle

Use Shuttle when your integration meets one or more of the following:

- Needs deterministic latency for short user-facing actions (<= 200ms median) and can accept lower-quality cached results for cold starts.
- Must run in a semi-disconnected context (mobile webviews, electron, or edge) with intermittent network to the Redwood hosted API.
- Requires an embeddings-first retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pattern with local cache and graceful degrade to smaller models or local heuristics.

Do not use Shuttle if you need server-side heavy throughput (high-concurrency batch generation) — prefer Dedicated endpoints.

Key components (terminology)

- Shuttle Host: minimal runtime wrapper (JS/Swift/Kotlin) included in client that routes calls to the local cache, edge prefetch, then Redwood API.
- Shuttle Adapter: the integration layer in your product code that translates app intents -> Redwood SDK calls and implements fallback policies.
- Local KV Cache: LRU-backed cache used for embedding vectors, KV prefixes, and small golden responses.
- Circuit Micro-batcher: groups small requests for the same session to reduce per-token overhead while respecting latency SLOs.

Quickstart (Javascript web embed)

1) Install and initialize (example uses the Shuttle host shim):

```bash
# npm
npm install @redwood/shuttle-host@latest
```

2) Bootstrap a Shuttle host instance and enable safe default policies:

```javascript
import { ShuttleHost } from '@redwood/shuttle-host';

const shuttle = new ShuttleHost({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_PUBLIC_KEY, // ephemeral token issued by server-side mint endpoint
  cacheSize: 1024, // number of vectors/objects
  circuitWindowMs: 40, // micro-batching window
  fallbackModel: 'redwood-small-v1',
  telemetryEnabled: true
});

await shuttle.start();
```

3) Example RAG flow with graceful degrade:

```javascript
// 1. request an embedding (local-first)
const embed = await shuttle.embed('user prompt');
// 2. nearest-neighbors in local index (fallback to server index)
const neighbors = shuttle.knnSearch(embed, { k: 10, threshold: 0.75});
if (neighbors.length < 3) {
  // escalate to server-side rerank (costlier) or use local heuristic
}
// 3. build a prompt with retrieved docs and stream generation with fallback
const stream = shuttle.generateStreaming({ model: 'redwood-rlm-l', prompt: builtPrompt });
stream.on('data', chunk => renderChunk(chunk));
stream.on('fallback', info => { showBanner('Degraded to cached or smaller model'); });
```

Recommended config table (defaults tuned for client UX)

| key | default | description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| cacheSize | 1024 | Max items in local KV cache (vectors + small generations). |
| cacheTTLSeconds | 3600 | Time-to-live for cached generative responses. |
| circuitWindowMs | 40 | Micro-batching window to group sibling calls from same session. |
| fallbackModel | redwood-small-v1 | Model used when primary model is unavailable. |
| streamingTimeoutMs | 8000 | Max time to wait for streaming response before fallback. |
| prefetchWindow | 3 | Number of tokens of user input to prefetch embeddings for typed input. |

Telemetry and observability

Shuttle emits a small set of structured events to the DevX telemetry pipeline (keys below are mandatory for Support reproducibility):

- shuttle.request_start -> { client_id, session_id, intent, trace_id }
- shuttle.cache_hit -> { cache_key, hit_ttl_seconds }
- shuttle.cache_miss -> { cache_key, reason }
- shuttle.fallback_trigger -> { fallback_type: 'model'|'network'|'timeout'|'cache', target }
- shuttle.generate_stream_metrics -> { latency_ms, tokens_streamed, final_model }

Instrument these at DEBUG level during early onramp. Telemetry cohorts we recommend: "shuttle-first-1000", "shuttle-cache-eviction-regressions". Attach golden traces (see appendix) to reproduce streaming deltas.

Rollout and migration checklist

1) Server-side mint endpoint: implement a short-lived token service so clients do not embed long-lived API keys. 2) Feature flag the Shuttle host in 10% of sessions for 48 hours with telemetry assertions. 3) After no regressions, expand to 50% and run a 72-hour golden trace comparison against non-Shuttle flows (latency, token-cost, quality metrics). 4) Full rollout with staged deprecation of older client adapters.

SLOs to validate during Canary

- Median interactive latency (user-visible generation start): <= 200ms 95th <= 750ms
- Cache hit ratio (initial user query): target >= 0.45 in active cohorts
- Fallback rate to smaller model or server: <= 8% after warmup

Canonical fixes for top support issues

1) Symptom: Streaming stalls mid-response after ~2–4s.
   - Root cause: circuitWindowMs set too high causing micro-batch flush delays under bursty input.
   - Fix: Lower circuitWindowMs to 20–30ms for interactive paths; increase streamingTimeoutMs to 10s for mobile slow networks.

2) Symptom: Cache returns stale or malformed generative output.
   - Root cause: cacheTTLSeconds longer than expected and prompt template evolved.
   - Fix: Invalidate cache by bumping cacheVersion in host config and redeploy; set cacheTTLSeconds to 3600 for generative templates and add content-hash to cache key.

3) Symptom: High fallback rate to smaller model after release.
   - Root cause: New primary model requires longer prefix lengths and exceeds token budget leading to early network timeouts.
   - Fix: Adjust token budget per-request, enable prefix-KV caching on host, and temporarily route affected sessions to a compatible model variant.

4) Symptom: Incorrect attribution in telemetry (mix of sessions).
   - Root cause: missing session_id propagation across webview and background workers.
   - Fix: Ensure shuttle.request_start is emitted synchronously when session is created and add session_id to localStorage signing.

Troubleshooting steps (fast triage)

1) Reproduce locally: use the Shuttle dev harness with the same cacheVersion and prefetchWindow.
2) Pull a golden trace for the failing session (trace_id in telemetry).
3) Compare token counts and model IDs between shuttle.generate_stream_metrics and server logs.
4) If fallback_type == 'network', capture client-side network waterfall and check TLS termination region mismatch.

Appendix A — Golden trace example

- trace_id: shuttle-gold-20260302-7a3b
- events: shuttle.request_start -> shuttle.cache_miss -> shuttle.generate_stream_metrics (latency_ms: 128, tokens_streamed: 54, final_model: redwood-rlm-l)

Appendix B — Example server mint endpoint (NodeJS)

```javascript
// Minimal minting endpoint; sign short lived key server-side and return to client
import express from 'express';
import { signEphemeral } from '@redwood/auth-utils';
const app = express();
app.post('/mint', async (req, res) => {
  const sessionId = req.body.session_id;
  const token = await signEphemeral({ sessionId, ttlSeconds: 60 });
  res.json({ token });
});
```

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: DevX SDK (team: eng-developer-experience)
- Secondary contact: Runtime Integration (team: eng-serving-runtime)
- Support escalation: open a labeled incident with team=devx-shuttle and include trace_id + client OS + cacheVersion
